label: input token j during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Token detector for j: fires on essentially every step where the input is j in the original phase (dev P=1.00, R=0.998). Never fires on any other input token, never on the delimiter, and essentially never in the copy phase (198 tiny activations), even when j is fed back as a copied input. Magnitude is largest when j is the first token (t=0, ~max 2.97) and decays with later original position (mean activation per step drops strongly from t=0 to t=8 per mass shares); repeated occurrences of j are weaker than the first occurrence (in_first=0 carries only 7% of mass, examples show 0.8-0.2 of max for second/third j).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test misses: 176 copy-phase activations holding 0.0% of mass. They are tiny (0.02 to 0.06 of max), mostly at step L+1 in sequences that start with j. There were 3 false positives, all a repeated j at t=8 right before <DEL>, which is scattered noise.
Copy phase: (phase==2)&(in_tok==j) has precision 0.002 and mass recall 0.00007 on test, so the claim that it 'almost never fires on copied j' holds.

Repeated j: (phase==0)&(in_tok==j)&(in_first==0) has precision 0.9998 and mass recall 0.069. Repeats almost always fire, just more weakly. The explanation's 'weaker' is about magnitude, not firing rate, so it is accurate.

Minor wording issue: the decline in activation 'share of mass' by t mostly reflects fewer steps at later positions (firing rate per original position is a flat ~0.033). The per-example magnitudes still show a real drop for late or repeated j. This does not change the verdict.
